title: Waymo: AI in the physical world powering the future of driving
description: Google I/O 2025 keynote conversation between Aditi Roy and Waymo Co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov. Details the 15-year history of autonomous driving from the early Google self-driving car project to serving over 250,000 weekly commercial driverless rides. Explores multimodal end-to-end foundation world models for physical reasoning, sensor fusion (LiDAR, radar, cameras), and statistical safety benchmarks surpassing human driving performance.

segments.heading: The imperative for autonomous mobility: road safety and human error
segments.text: Every 26 seconds, a person loses their life in a motor vehicle collision worldwide, totaling over 1.3 million annual deaths, with the overwhelming majority caused by human distraction, impairment, and error. Dmitri Dolgov describes Waymo's founding mission over 15 years ago to eliminate traffic fatalities by building the world's most experienced and trusted autonomous driver.

segments.heading: Scaling commercial operations: 250,000+ weekly driverless rides
segments.text: Waymo transitioned from experimental research into commercial urban mobility, operating fully driverless ride-hailing services across major metropolitan areas (Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Austin) and delivering over 250,000 paid passenger trips every week with industry-leading customer satisfaction.

segments.heading: Physical AI and foundation world models for autonomous driving
segments.text: Operating in physical reality requires reasoning through dense traffic, adverse weather, unpredictable pedestrians, and complex construction zones. Waymo integrates multimodal foundation world models developed in partnership with Google DeepMind, transforming multi-sensor inputs (custom LiDAR, imaging radar, surround cameras) into predictive physical simulations and safe vehicle trajectories.

segments.heading: Empirical safety data and the 6th-generation Waymo Driver
segments.text: Over tens of millions of commercial driverless miles, Waymo vehicles demonstrate an 85% reduction in injury-causing crashes compared to human drivers in the same geographies. Dolgov previews the 6th-generation Waymo Driver, which reduces system costs, enhances cold-weather performance, and accelerates global fleet expansion.
